text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswana press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A traditional healer at Makgwelekgwe, 55 kilometres from Maun, claims to have found a cure for AIDS. The cure involves a mixture of traditional medicine and surgery on the anus and genitalia of affected persons.
- The hydrology department has predicted this year's Okavango River flood, which feeds the delta, will be higher than last year.
- Namibia is reported to be preparing to pull out of the Common Market for East and Southern Africa (COMESA).
- Farmers who sell their cattle to the Botswana Meat Commission can expect record prices, BMT chairman Martin Mannathoko said.
